summary:
Cosmic Tracker is an interactive web platform built for the NASA SPHEREx Challenge to bridge the gap between complex astrophysical data and human curiosity by visualizing the user journey across the cosmos. NASA’s SPHEREx mission surveys the entire sky in near-infrared light to uncover the origins of the universe, galaxies, and life-sustaining water in planetary systems. However, raw spectroscopic and astronomical datasets from archives like IRSA, Gaia, and NEOSSat are often difficult for students, educators, and space enthusiasts to interpret.

Cosmic Tracker transforms these multi-dimensional datasets into an intuitive, story-driven visual journey. Instead of navigating static tables, users embark on a guided cosmic exploration—tracking how infrared light travels from distant galaxies and interstellar ices to space telescopes, and interacting with real celestial coordinates, spectral signatures, and 3D spatial maps. 

By integrating open-source datasets from NASA’s SPHEREx and NEOWISE archives alongside Canadian Space Agency (NEOSSat) and ESA (Gaia) resources, our platform democratizes space science. Cosmic Tracker makes deep-space spectroscopy accessible, educational, and engaging, inspiring the next generation of explorers to understand our cosmic origins through interactive data visualization.
details: What it does & How it works: Cosmic Tracker is an interactive web platform designed specifically for the NASA SPHEREx challenge. It ingests and parses raw spectroscopic and astronomical data from missions like SPHEREx, Gaia, and NEOSSat, transforming complex numbers into an engaging, story-driven "user journey." Users can navigate an interactive 2D/3D interface that simulates traveling through the near-infrared universe, allowing them to trace how light and celestial bodies are mapped across the sky, examine spectral signatures, and explore cosmic coordinates dynamically. Benefits & Intended Impact: The project democratizes astrophysics. It bridges the gap between complex scientific archives and public curiosity. By turning dense astronomical data into an accessible and visual exploration, Cosmic Tracker empowers students, educators, and space enthusiasts to learn about the origins of the universe, galaxies, and water without needing a PhD in astrophysics. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, & Software Used: - Frontend: React.js, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (for 3D space and journey visualizations). - Backend & Data Processing: Python, Flask, Pandas, and Astropy. - Data Sources & Archives: NASA SPHEREx Mission Archive, ESA Gaia Archive, and Canadian Space Agency (NEOSSat) datasets. - AI/Super Intelligence (SI) Tools: Utilized Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist with code optimization, debugging, and structuring educational descriptive metadata (fully acknowledged per challenge guidelines). Creativity & Design Considerations: We focused on "gamifying" and humanizing data exploration. Instead of presenting users with static tables or boring charts, Cosmic Tracker turns data analysis into an immersive adventure. We carefully considered UI/UX design to ensure smooth performance in browser-based 3D environments, making space science visually stunning, intuitive, and interactive for all age groups.
